# QC13: 含晖楼 Hanhui Lou

Wave 4 · Qichun Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=QC13` · Page: `/scenes/#QC13` · Row: `research/buildings/QC13-hanhui-lou/`

## What it was

含晖楼 Hanhui Lou, in the south-west of Qichun Yuan on the site of the old 含晖园 (given to Prince Yongxuan about 1773, to Princess Zhuangjing 1801, returned 1811 as 南园), when the tower 联辉楼 was moved here from 西爽村: a two-storey tower of seven bays with a riding track (撒马道) and lawn in front for mounted archery (E0722, E0705, E0718, E0720). The Thirty Scenes call it 含光楼, 'the old 联辉楼' (S223; E0448). Daoguang held lantern viewing and banquets here with the dowager (E0719, E1186); the emperor passed it in 1856 (E1524).

From the inventory row: **built** by 1812 (first dated item); **changed** Used for Lantern Festival banquets under Daoguang and on the 1856 route; 聯暉樓 (Prince Cheng, 西爽村) > 含光樓 (in the Thirty Scenes, 1805) > 含晖楼; S224 adds that Jiaqing moved the tower after 1811; 1811: 联辉楼 moved here from 西爽村, called 含辉楼; **destroyed** 1860 (S06, S49, S01, S210, S223, S224, S360, S361).
